rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before any outcome; synthetic validation with heterogeneous, flat and selection worlds on the real G51 design; replication on the two eligible periods (G51, G38) for three outcomes; 2 natives (NE43 selection check, NE44 shape); 30 estimate rows; confirm.py frozen and dry-run, not run. Only two periods are eligible.
rationale.faithfulness: The index claim fails: on active calls the index does not beat the logged nudger (x1.08 [-0.30, 3.44]) or once-early (x0.69), the read-out clock adds nothing, and NE44's shape flip fails. The sustained-escape gain (x2.36) is the kind the synthetic selection world fakes. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: Gives a concrete, replicated operator rule: nudge each idle trap once at its second gate (x1.55 [1.25, 1.81] over the logged nudger; random choice already beats it x1.46). Also prices the lever: a gate nudge adds 7.2 active calls, but the nudger's total is 0.19% of the swarm's calls. Rules out building a fancier index.

one_line: A Gittins-style nudge index does not beat once-early; the logged nudger is worse than random gate choice (x1.46), and once-early beats it x1.55.
